chapterTag.category: AP Calc BC BC-2 — Logistic & Euler's Method

body.en: Unit 7BC · Logistic Models & Euler's Method covers essential College Board AP Calculus BC competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Logistic Differential Equation & Carrying Capacity

body.en: Understand the logistic model \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP(L - P)\) or \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP(1 - P/L)\), where \(L\) is the carrying capacity.
Carrying capacity \(L\): \(\lim_{t\to\infty} P(t) = L\). Maximum growth rate occurs when \(P = L/2\). The point of inflection occurs at \(P = L/2\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

A population satisfies \(\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.002P(600 - P)\). What is the carrying capacity \(L\), and at what population size is the growth rate maximized?

solution.en: The carrying capacity is \(L = 600\). The growth rate \(\frac{dP}{dt}\) is maximized at half the carrying capacity: \(P = 600 / 2 = \mathbf{300}\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Euler's Method Step-by-Step Numerical Approximations

body.en: Apply the iterative formula \(y_{n+1} = y_n + f(x_n, y_n)\Delta x\) with uniform step sizes.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Let \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y\) with initial condition \(y(0) = 1\). Use Euler's method with 2 steps of size \(\Delta x = 0.5\) to approximate \(y(1)\).

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Euler Error Over/Under-Estimation & Analytic Logistic Solutions

body.en: Analyze whether Euler's method overestimates or underestimates based on concavity (second derivative), and solve logistic equations using separation of variables.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Suppose \(y(x)\) satisfies a differential equation where \(y'' > 0\) on the interval \([a, b]\). Does Euler's method produce an overestimate or underestimate of \(y(b)\)? Justify.

solution.en: Because \(y'' > 0\), the solution curve \(y(x)\) is concave up. Tangent lines lie below a concave-up curve. Since Euler's method follows tangent line segments, it will produce an underestimate of the true value \(y(b)\).
